text: もう　たまらん　ほど　つりが　すき　なんだが　きみは　つり　すき　かな？

structure.jp: もう　たまらん　ほど
structure.en: so much I can't stand it

structure.jp: つりが　すき　なんだが
きみは　つり　すき　かな？
structure.en: do you like fishing, I wonder?

patterns.name: 〜ほど
patterns.explanation: ほど means 'to the point that' and shows how strong something is. たまらん is the old-man form of たまらない. たまらん　ほど　すき = 'like it so much I can't stand it'.

patterns.name: 〜のだ
patterns.explanation: んだ, short for のだ, adds the feeling of explaining yourself: 'the thing is'. すき　なんだ = 'the thing is, I love it'.

patterns.name: 〜が (but)
patterns.explanation: が at the end of a part of a sentence means 'but'. Here it is soft and just leads into the question. すき　なんだが　きみは = 'I love it, but what about you'.
